stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A large mass creates an attractive gravitational field around it — the field pulls inward and weakens with distance. Sweep the source mass $M$ and the probe distance $r$ and watch how the field magnitude at the probe changes. Advance when both sliders have covered at least half of their range.
stages.concept: Newton's law of gravitation: $|\vec{\mathcal{G}}| = \dfrac{G\,M}{r^{2}}$, with $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{N\,m^{2}/kg^{2}}$. The field points radially toward the source. Doubling $M$ doubles the field; halving $r$ quadruples it. Units: $\mathrm{N/kg} \equiv \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$ — the same quantity described as force per unit mass or as acceleration.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A dashed target ring marks the radius $r^{*}$ and the target field magnitude $|\vec{\mathcal{G}^{*}}|$. Slide the probe out to $r = r^{*}$, then tune the source mass $M$ until the field magnitude at the probe matches the target.
stages.concept: $|\vec{\mathcal{G}^{*}}| = \dfrac{G\,M^{*}}{r^{*2}}\ \Rightarrow\ M^{*} = \dfrac{|\vec{\mathcal{G}^{*}}|\,r^{*2}}{G}$. One field magnitude at a fixed radius fixes the source mass exactly — no free variable to play with.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The field heatmap is hidden. Only the target ring at $r^{*}$ with its label $|\vec{\mathcal{G}^{*}}|$ remains. Compute the source mass $M^{*}$ on paper, then set both sliders to your computed values and submit. One submit per setup — an incorrect answer rotates to a new target.
stages.concept: Inverse formula: $M^{*} = \dfrac{|\vec{\mathcal{G}^{*}}|\,r^{*2}}{G}$. Work in SI: convert $r^{*}$ from $\mathrm{Mm}$ to metres ($\times 10^{6}$). Express the answer in $10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$ (Earth mass $\approx 5.97 \times 10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$).

labels.tip1: sweep M and r across at least half their ranges
labels.tip2: place the probe on the target ring, then tune M
labels.tip3: compute M on paper first, then set both sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: |g| = G*M / r^2  =>  M = |g*| * r*^2 / G. Plug the target values in directly.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: G ~ 6.67e-11. Convert r* from Mm to m (x 1e6). Answer scales in units of 10^24 kg.

1.1: Which slider has the stronger effect on |g| — mass or distance? Try halving r.
1.2: |g| grows linearly with M but as 1/r^2 with distance. Halving r quadruples |g|.
1.3: Sweep each slider from its minimum all the way to its maximum to hit the 50% coverage bar on both.

2.1: Read the target labels near the dashed ring: r* is the radius, |g*| is the field magnitude.
2.2: First move the probe to r = r*. With r fixed, M alone controls |g|.
2.3: Solve directly: M = |g*| * r*^2 / G. Plug the on-screen numbers into this formula.

3.1: The heatmap is gone but the formula still holds. Write |g*| = G*M*/r*^2 on paper.
3.2: Rearrange to M* = |g*| * r*^2 / G. Convert r* from Mm to metres (multiply by 1e6) before you square it.
3.3: Peek reveals the exact rearrangement. Apply it to the r* and |g*| shown on screen, then read the result in units of 10^24 kg.
